source.title: Some open problems in Banach space theory

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional Banach space X such that every bounded linear operator T: X → X can be written in the form T = λI + K, where λ is a scalar, I is the identity operator on X, and K is a compact operator?

evidence.quote: (Q.1) Does there exist an infinite dimensional Banach space X so that every bounded linear operator T : X -> X is of the form T = λI + K with K compact ?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X and Y such that every compact linear operator from X to Y is nuclear?

evidence.quote: (Q.2) Does there exist a pair of infinite dimensional Banach spaces X and Y so that every compact operator from X to Y is nuclear ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be an infinite-dimensional uniformly convex Banach space. Does there exist a constant C such that for every positive integer n there is a subspace Y_n ⊂ X with Banach-Mazur distance d(Y_n, ℓ₂^n) ≤ C and a bounded projection P_n: X → Y_n with ||P_n|| ≤ C?
accepted.context_brief: local theory and complemented ℓ₂^n copies

evidence.quote: (Q.3) Let X be an infinite-dimensional uniformly convex Banach space. Does there exist a constant C so that for every n there is a subspace Yn ⊂ X so that d(Yn , l2n) ≤ C and there is a projection Pn : X -> Yn with ||Pn|| ≤ C ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. Does there exist a constant C and an exponent p ∈ {1, 2, ∞} such that for every positive integer n there is a subspace Y_n ⊂ X with d(Y_n, ℓ_p^n) ≤ C and a bounded projection P_n from X onto Y_n with ||P_n|| ≤ C?
accepted.context_brief: local theory for general Banach spaces

evidence.quote: (Q.4) Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. Does there exist a constant C and a p0 (equal either to 1, 2 or ∞) so that for every n there is a subspace Yn ⊂ X with d(Yn , lpn) ≤ C and a projection Pn from X on to Yn with ||Pn|| ≤ C ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Banach space such that the quotient X**/X is not reflexive, where X** is the bidual of X under the canonical embedding of X into X**. Is it true that for every ε > 0 and every positive integer n there is a subspace Y of X with Banach-Mazur distance d(Y, ℓ₁^n) ≤ 1 + ε? In particular, what happens for n = 5?

evidence.quote: (Q.5) Let X be a Banach space such that X**/X is not reflexive. Is it true that for every ε and every integer n there is a subspace Y of X with d(Y , l1n) ≤ 1 + ε ? In particular, what is the situation for n = 5 ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space that is not isomorphic to a Hilbert space. Must X contain a subspace that fails the approximation property (AP)?

evidence.quote: (Q.6) Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space which is not isomorphic to a Hilbert space. Does X have a subspace which fails to have the AP ?

accepted.question_text: Does B(ℓ₂), the Banach space of all bounded linear operators from ℓ₂ to itself equipped with the operator norm, have the approximation property? Also, does the Banach space of all bounded analytic functions f(z) on the unit disc {z : |z| < 1}, equipped with the supremum norm, have the approximation property?
accepted.context_brief: AP for operator and analytic-function spaces

evidence.quote: (Q.7) Let B(l2) be the space of all bounded operators from l2 into itself with the operator norm. Does B(l2) have the AP ? Does the space of all bounded analytic functions f(z) on {z ; |z| < 1} with the sup norm have the AP ?

accepted.question_text: Does C(ℓ₂), the Banach space of compact operators on ℓ₂ with the usual operator norm, have the uniform approximation property (UAP)? Also, does the disc algebra have the uniform approximation property?

evidence.quote: (Q.8) Does the space C(l2) (the space of compact operators on l2 with the usual operator norm) have the UAP ? Does the disc algebra have the UAP ?

accepted.question_text: If a Banach space X has the uniform approximation property, must its dual space X* also have the uniform approximation property?

evidence.quote: (Q.9) Let X have the UAP; does X* have the UAP ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. Does X contain an infinite-dimensional subspace with an unconditional basis?

evidence.quote: (Q.10) Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. Does X have an infinite-dimensional subspace with an unconditional basis ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. Does X contain an infinite-dimensional subspace Y such that Y is either reflexive or isomorphic to c₀ or to ℓ₁?

evidence.quote: (Q.11) Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. Does X contain an infinite-dimensional subspace Y so that Y is either reflexive or isomorphic to one of the spaces c0 and l1 ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Banach space that has at least two non-equivalent symmetric bases. Must X then have infinitely many mutually non-equivalent symmetric bases?

evidence.quote: (Q.12) Let X be a Banach space having at least two non equivalent symmetric bases. Must X have infinitely many mutually non equivalent symmetric bases ?

accepted.question_text: If X and Y are uniformly homeomorphic Banach spaces, must X and Y be isomorphic as Banach spaces?

evidence.quote: (Q.13) Let X and Y be two uniformly homeomorphic Banach spaces. Is X isomorphic to Y ?

accepted.question_text: Is the Hilbert space ℓ₂ uniformly homeomorphic to a bounded subset of itself?

evidence.quote: (Q.14) Is the Hilbert space l2 uniformly homeomorphic to a bounded subset of itself ?

accepted.question_text: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space X have an infinite-dimensional separable quotient space?

evidence.quote: (Q.15) Does every infinitely dimensional Banach space X have an infinite dimensional separable quotient space ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Banach space that is Lindelöf in its weak topology. Must X be isomorphic to a subspace of a weakly compactly generated (WCG) Banach space?

evidence.quote: (Q.16) Let X be a Banach space. Assume that X is a Lindelöf space in its w topology; is X isomorphic to a subspace of a WCG space ?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a compact Hausdorff space. Does there exist a totally disconnected compact Hausdorff space K₀ such that the Banach spaces C(K) and C(K₀) are isomorphic?

evidence.quote: (Q.17) Let K be a compact Hausdorff space. Does there exist a totally disconnected compact Hausdorff space K0 so that C(K) ≈ C(K0) ?

accepted.question_text: Characterize the Banach spaces that admit an equivalent strictly convex norm, meaning an equivalent norm ||·|| such that whenever ||x|| = ||y|| = 1 and ||x + y|| = 2, one must have x = y.

evidence.quote: (Q.18) Characterize those Banach spaces which have an equivalent strictly convex norm.
A norm is strictly convex if ||x|| = ||y|| = 1 and ||x + y|| = 2 imply that x = y .
